data.title: Fed Minutes: Vast Majority of Officials See Upside Inflation Risks
data.description: According to Jin10, minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting showed that most FOMC members expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term before gradually declining to 2% over time. However, amid high energy prices and continued constraints on refined-fuel supplies, a “vast majority” of officials saw upside risks to the inflation outlook. Many officials also viewed AI infrastructure development as an important source of inflation risk. Most said costs driven by AI construction and related investment could broadly pass through to consumer-goods and business-services prices and persist for an extended period.

data.title: FOMC Minutes | Fed Minutes Due Today: Two October Dissents Favored a Hike as Markets Price 97% Odds for December
data.description:
The Federal Reserve releases minutes from its October 27–28 policy meeting at 2:00 p.m. ET (19:00 UTC) on Wednesday, November 18. Investors will look for how much support there is for a December rate hike. At that meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee held the federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Markets now price a 97% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed’s December 9 meeting, according to CME FedWatch.
Fed Held Rates at 3.75%–4.00% After September’s Hike
The October decision paused the Fed’s tightening after September’s rate increase, its first hike since 2023. In its statement, the committee said economic activity “is expanding at a strong pace.” It cited resilient domestic spending, strong productivity growth and robust capital investment. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

On prices, the Fed said that “inflation remains elevated.” It said gathering more information would help it set the policy needed to ensure “a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s 2 percent goal,” and added: “The Committee will deliver price stability.”
Two Officials Dissented in Favor of an Immediate Hike
Cook and Hammack voted against the decision, preferring to raise the target range by 0.25 percentage point in October. Two dissents in favor of tighter policy signal that part of the committee already saw a case for further hikes before the latest inflation data.
The minutes will show how widely that view was shared among the 19 officials who take part in the discussion, including those without a vote this year. Traders will watch for language such as “many” or “most participants” supporting further increases, which would back the December hike now priced in.

Fed Rate Settings Stay Unchanged
Alongside the decision, the Fed kept its other policy rates in place, effective October 29:
Interest on reserve balances: 3.90%Standing overnight repo rate: 4.00%Overnight reverse repo rate: 3.75%, with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion a dayPrimary credit rate: 4.00%
The Fed also said it would keep buying Treasury bills, and if needed other Treasuries maturing within three years, to maintain ample bank reserves. It is rolling over all maturing Treasury holdings and reinvesting agency securities payments into Treasury bills.
Hawkish Comments Lift Hike Bets Ahead of the Minutes
Since the October meeting, policymakers have sounded more hawkish. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has said he is very concerned that inflation is moving in the wrong direction, according to reports. He said the Fed may need either a 50-basis-point hike or a clear signal of tighter policy.
The US Dollar Index rose 0.3% to 103.91 on Wednesday, its highest since April 2025. Gold fell 2% to about $3,772 an ounce, and bitcoin traded near $64,000 as expectations of higher rates weighed on assets that pay no yield.
What the Minutes Could Mean for Markets
Minutes that show broad support for a December hike would confirm current pricing and could keep the dollar strong. If they reveal debate over a larger 50-basis-point move, rate expectations could shift further toward tightening, weighing on risk assets including stocks and crypto. Minutes that show more caution, for example about slowing growth or recent declines in oil prices, could ease some of that pressure.

data.title: Nvidia Interim CEO Colette Kress Tells Employees ‘Let’s Move Forward’ at First All-Hands Since Jensen Huang Resigned
data.description: According to CNBC, interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress told employees “let’s move forward” Wednesday at the company’s first all-hands meeting since founder Jensen Huang resigned. Kress also raised employee pay increases, and board chair Harvey Jones discussed the search for a new CEO, according to attendees. The meeting was held in person and streamed on Microsoft Teams. Nvidia shares fell 2% Wednesday, a day after the company reported third-quarter earnings that topped Wall Street expectations. Bernstein and Evercore were among the firms that downgraded the stock that day.

data.title: Jaan Tallinn Could Reap Tens of Billions in Anthropic IPO
data.description: According to CNBC, Jaan Tallinn could make tens of billions of dollars from Anthropic’s planned IPO, although his exact stake has not been disclosed. Tallinn led the company’s $124 million Series A funding round. Anthropic is set to list on the Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT, at an expected valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion. Tallinn’s potential return depends on dilution in later funding rounds and whether he sold any shares.

data.title: Binance Secures ADGM Court Order to Support Recovery of Assets From 29 October Attack
data.description: Binance Blog published a new article, providing an update on efforts to recover assets linked to the 29 October security incident. Today, Binance said it had obtained a court order in the Abu Dhabi Global Markets (ADGM) Courts to support recovery of assets connected to the attack. The company said the order is part of its effort to use lawful means to recover stolen assets and prevent funds from reaching attackers or people facilitating the attack. Binance said it had absorbed the financial impact of the stolen funds so users would not bear the cost, while also pursuing the assets, supporting law enforcement and industry partners, and seeking to recover frozen funds through legal channels. The company noted that issuers, exchanges or other partners may require a formal court order before frozen assets can be released, transferred or returned. Binance said it is working with law enforcement and relevant authorities, coordinating with issuers, exchanges, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners, and tracing and monitoring assets connected to the attack. It is also supporting asset freezes and recovery where legally possible, and taking formal legal steps to reclaim assets already frozen or identified in the future. Binance said the process will take time and that it plans to provide updates as recovery efforts progress.

data.title: Ondo to Launch Tokenized Anthropic Stock on IPO Day
data.description: Ondo Finance plans to launch ANTon, a token tied to Anthropic shares, on Thursday, when the AI company is slated to begin trading on Nasdaq. The token will be available to eligible investors outside the U.S., according to The Block, and tracks ANT share prices without direct stock ownership. Anthropic is expected to set its IPO price after market close on Wednesday; analysts project up to $90 billion at the top of the range, potentially topping SpaceX’s $85.7 billion June IPO. Ondo says minting and redemption will run 24/7, with waived minting fees and reduced redemption fees for an unspecified period. ANTon will join more than 450 tokenized stocks and ETFs on Ondo Stocks, which Ondo says has surpassed $1 billion in total value locked.

data.title: MARA Prices $185M Debt Offering After $1.1B Bitcoin Sale
data.description:
Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings has priced a $185 million secured debt offering through its U.S. subsidiary to help finance its $1.5 billion acquisition of Long Ridge Energy & Power. According to Cointelegraph, a Tuesday filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said the notes carry an 8.75% interest rate and mature in 2032. They will be added to $600 million in existing Long Ridge notes at the same rate, bringing the combined principal to $785 million and annual interest obligations to about $68.7 million. The offering is expected to close on Nov. 27, alongside the acquisition. Long Ridge operates a 485-megawatt natural gas power plant in Ohio. MARA announced the acquisition on April 30 as part of its expansion into AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. The property includes land that MARA says could support more than 1 gigawatt of data center capacity, though the company has not announced a major AI tenant for the proposed development.

The financing follows MARA’s Nov. 9 disclosure that it sold 13,597 Bitcoin after quarter-end for approximately $1.1 billion. The company used $750 million to repay Bitcoin-backed loans, freeing 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral. In March, MARA sold 15,133 BTC for approximately $1.1 billion and used the proceeds to help repurchase $1 billion in convertible notes at a roughly 9% discount, saving approximately $88 million before transaction costs. In its Nov. 9 shareholder letter, the company said it had reduced debt by approximately $1.4 billion, or 37%, since the beginning of the year, although the Long Ridge deal will add debt to its consolidated balance sheet. Long Ridge generated approximately $144 million in annualized adjusted EBITDA, extrapolated from the second half of 2025, according to MARA’s April 30 acquisition announcement. Holders of approximately $924 million in convertible notes can demand repayment in 2027, according to the company’s third-quarter 10-Q. MARA shares traded at $6.57 at 6:53 pm UTC on Wednesday, up 2.34% on the day but down 46% over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance data.
